name: Offline time stretch
threading: Worker thread only. Pure functions with no shared state, so concurrent calls on independent inputs are safe. Never call from the audio thread.
platforms: Any C++17 compiler. Built with -ffp-contract=off (GCC/Clang) or /fp:precise (MSVC): the same binary gives bit-identical output; across compilers expect agreement within 1e-5.
standalone_test_command: cmake -S modules/time_stretch -B build/time_stretch && cmake --build build/time_stretch && ctest --test-dir build/time_stretch
summary: Offline WSOLA time stretching of planar float audio (1 or 2 channels) in chop-anchored regions, three quality presets (Draft, Standard, High), progress and cancel, and the exact integer marker scaling rule that keeps chop boundaries on their scaled positions without drift. No third-party code; decoding, tempo detection, and UI are adapters.
public_api: `mapPosition(pos, in, out)` / `mapLength(len, in, out)`: floor((2*p*out + in) / (2*in)) computed from the original value, so scaled markers never drift
`makePlan(inFrames, outFrames, anchors)`: sorted, de-duplicated region plan with 0 and inFrames added
`stretch(Input, Plan, Quality, Progress)`: planar result of exactly `plan.outFrames` frames per channel; returns `Cancelled` when the progress callback returns false
limits: Length ratio 0.5 to 2.0 inclusive; frame counts up to 2,000,000,000 per side; 1 or 2 channels; 8 kHz to 384 kHz
Regions shorter than three analysis windows (one drum hit) are copied with a 5 ms fade instead of stretched
Non-finite input samples are read as 0; output is always finite
adapters: The composition root builds the plan from chop markers and runs stretch on a worker; tempo (source BPM) comes from the user or from clip duration, never from the audio.
adapter_notes: Hand in decoded planar float buffers and region anchors in source frames; scale your own marker data with mapPosition/mapLength using the same (in, out) pair.
removal: Remove the composition root's stretch API (composition/src/stretch.cpp) and the Tempo match section of the editor first; no other module depends on this one.
